description.narrative: (Bangladesh): Bangladesh is a source, destination, and transit country for forced labor and human trafficking. Widespread poverty, unemployment, corruption, poor governance, porous borders, and traditional gender inequities fuel trafficking. The 2024 Department of State Trafficking in Persons (TIP) report kept Bangladesh at Tier Two, stressing the urgent need for the Government of Bangladesh (GoB) to allocate more resources to counter trafficking and fully comply with the Trafficking Victims Protection Act (TVPA). The high rate of child marriage (CM) is concerning, with 52 percent of girls marrying before 18, leaving them vulnerable to trafficking.With FY 2024 funds, USAID's Fight Slavery and Trafficking in Persons (FSTIP) activity will expand partnerships with civil society and the private sector to strengthen comprehensive protection mechanisms for those at risk and survivors of trafficking and CM. FSTIP will engage the GoB, youth, civil society organizations, and community members to prevent human rights violations and raise awareness of TIP and CM. It will also enhance judicial and law enforcement capacity to bring perpetrators to justice, supporting the GoB-led National Plan of Action and the Prevention and Suppression of Human Trafficking Act of 2012. FSTIP will also support the implementation of several recommendations outlined in the 2024 TIP report for GoB.This IM contributes to the Women, Peace and Security earmark ($200k), Trafficking in Persons ($300k), and Mental Health and Psychosocial Support ($100k). The activity is in line with the Integrated Country Strategy Mission Objective 1.1 - Bangladesh is more capable of protecting its sovereignty, population, and borders, combating terrorism, and countering violent extremism and USAID's CDCS Mission Development Objective 1 - Democracy Strengthened for an Inclusive Society.
